statement.p: If \mbox{curl }\vec F=(x^2+z^2)\vec j +5\vec k, find \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r, where C is a circle of radius 2, centered at the origin, with
(a) C in the xy-plane, oriented counterclockwise when viewed from above.
(b) C in the xz-plane, oriented counterclockwise when viewed from the positive y-axis.

static.solution:
(a) We use Stokes' theorem, with S the interior of the circle in the xy-plane, oriented upward. Then \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S\mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_S((x^2+z^2)\vec j + 5\vec k)\cdot d\vec A. Since d\vec A=\vec k \,dA, we have \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S 5\,dA =5\cdot\hbox{ Area of } S = 20\pi.
(b) Using Stokes' theorem again, this time with S as the interior of the circle in the xz-plane, we have \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S\mbox{curl }\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_S((x^2+z^2)\vec j +5 \vec k)\cdot d\vec A. Since d\vec A = \vec j\,dx\,dz, only the \vec j component of \mbox{curl }\vec F contributes to the flux. Thus, converting to polar coordinates gives \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_S(x^2+z^2)\,dx\,dz = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{2} r^2\,r\,dr\,d\theta = 2\pi\frac{r^4}4\bigg|_0^{2} = 8\pi.
